note: Each row is the average amount one kind of firm lent the Federal Reserve overnight through its reverse repo facility, over the business days of the month: the firm hands over cash and holds Treasuries from the Fed until the next morning. Government-sponsored enterprises are mostly the Federal Home Loan Banks. Money market funds park cash here when the Fed pays at least as much as other safe overnight lending, so when these amounts fall that cash has gone into Treasury bills or private lending, which is why it counts as liquidity. The average is used rather than the last day because amounts jump at the end of each month and quarter. The New York Fed publishes the split by lender about six weeks after each operation, so the book ends in the latest month where every day has it, and the totals for the 30 business days since, to 14 September 2026, are in the full table. This is not the separate pool the Fed runs for foreign central banks. Source: Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
